newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices recover as Germany and Iran fall out.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices recover as Germany and Iran fall out.

text.p: World oil prices ended firmer on Thursday, rallying off new nine-month lows amid signs of rising tension between the European Union and Iran over the killing of four Kurdish exiles in Germany.

A German court ruling implicating Tehran in the 1992 Berlin restaurant killings provoked a round of tit-for-tat diplomatic expulsions and an invitation from the EU for members to withdraw their ambassadors to Iran for consultations.

While the dispute would have no immediate impact on oil supply from Iran, a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and the world's third largest oil exporter behind Saudi Arabia and Norway, it could force the EU to drop its opposition to U.S. trade santions against Tehran.
Attempts to improve relations between Iran and its Gulf neighbours could also suffer, analysts said.

"In the short term this has no impact on oil supply but in the long run it is not only a setback for Iran but possibly also for the region as a whole," said Mehdi Varzi, oil analyst at finance house Kleinwort Benson.
London May Brent Blend crude futures closed 18 cents firmer at $17.95 a barrel, 64 cents above the early nine-month low posted as dealers focussed on ample supplies of crude oil and gasoline.
Traders said prices had yet to reflect predicted extra demand gasoline to fuel the summer U.S. driving season.
"Gasoline has proved disappointing so far. There's no sign yet of any concerns over a shortage of gasoline in the U.S..." one trader said.

Rising Iraqi exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal were also keeping up pressure on prices. Iraqi sales are now thought to be running close to 800,000 barrels a day (bpd), up from just over 500,000 bpd early in the year.
The extra sales are needed for Baghdad to meet a permitted $2 billion target by the end of June.
The United Nations approved a further four oil sale contracts on Wednesday and now has authorised a total of 44 contracts worth a total of +$16 billion.
But the row in relations between Tehran and its main trading partner was enough to push prices higher again on Thursday.
"People have been looking at the recall of European ambassadors from Iran and the possible implications of that," said a broker.
The European Union has refused to join U.S. trade sanctions on Iran and has attacked U.S. legislation providing for measures against firms that invest in its oil or gas industry.
Washington welcomed the German court ruling as a victory for its efforts to persuade Germany to take a tougher line with Tehran and it called on the European Union to adopt sanctions.
